searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight for chunk h4, none of them the author's; two left unspent. Four were restricted to the house's or the Union's own domain and read through their summaries. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the people and their dates, the village, the kind of producer, every change of hands, the grapes, the sites, the first vintage, the lees, the dosage, the bottle, the other cuvées, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries.

tested.founded: 1910 by the library and the Union's house profile; 1522 as the family's symbolic date, by the house. Confirmed.
tested.story: The Union's chronology: the son-in-law succeeded on the death of the head of the house in 1963, the Gosset owners took a majority 1980 to 1987, the house was a subsidiary of the Marie Brizard group 1987 to 1997 (the Hachette guide gives 1987 as well), and the Boizel Chanoine Champagne group bought it in 1997. The record had the son-in-law running it until 1987 and left Marie Brizard out: fixed. The perpetual reserve from 1946: the house. The 1951 as the first sold under a Clos label: Decanter alone, cut. The 1912 purchase of the Vallet cellars was not returned by this refuter's searches and stays on the author's reading.
tested.style: Réserve Perpétuelle, formerly Royale Réserve: the house and a merchant. The oak and malolactic shares: the house's sheets. Confirmed.
tested.cuvee: 85 per cent Pinot Noir for the 2013 and 78 for the 2015, 4.25 grams a litre, nine years in the cellar for the 2015, 64 per cent in wood and no malolactic for the 2014: the house. Walled: the house says a wall has enclosed it since 1887, Decanter calls it walled. 5.83 hectares by the house, 5.5 by Decanter and the Union. Goisses from a local word for a very steep slope: two accounts. Made almost every year since 1935: the house. Juste Rosé named for its pale colour: Decanter alone, cut; the 2012 sold, by two merchants.
tested.table: cuvee45 gave the slope sun from sunrise to sunset, a claim no source read carries, and served it at 10 to 12 degrees against cuvee.serve's 9 to 12: both fixed.
tested.cards: Three cards and three questions read: one right answer each, plausible wrong ones (Le Clos Saint-Hilaire, Grande Sendrée, Le Mesnil; 1910, 1935, 1987), no length clue. The house question's stem leaned on the trade union's chronology, a misnamed body: cut before the freeze.

changes.was: his son-in-law ran it from 1963 to 1987, and between 1980 and 1987 the family of the Gosset house took a majority holding
changes.now: his son-in-law succeeded him in 1963, and from 1980 to 1987 the owners of the Gosset house held a majority of its shares. From 1987 the house belonged to the Marie Brizard group
changes.why: The chronology dates the son-in-law's succession and the Gosset majority, and the Marie Brizard group's years 1987 to 1997; it gives no end of the son-in-law's years at 1987.
sources: Union des Maisons de Champagne: chronologie, Maison Philipponnat

changes.was: In the 1950s the wine took the name Clos des Goisses, and the 1951 was the first sold under a Clos label, by Decanter.
changes.now: cut; first.what says the house first bottled its wine alone in 1935
changes.why: One secondary account; the brief asks for two or one primary.

changes.was: by the trade union's chronology; 1987 the end of the Gosset family's majority holding
changes.now: no source in the stem; 1987 the year the house joined the Marie Brizard group
changes.why: The Union des Maisons de Champagne is the houses' own body, not a trade union, and a stem needs no source; the option of 1987 now teaches the change of hands the record tells. The keys are not frozen.
sources: Union des Maisons de Champagne: chronologie, Maison Philipponnat

changes.was: Made as a vintage wine in the years the house chooses, from the 1935 on; ... and the house shows the 2013, 2014 and 2015.
changes.now: Made almost every year since the 1935, by the house's own account; ... and the 2013, 2014 and 2015 are among its vintages.
changes.why: The house says the collection is almost uninterrupted since 1935; what the house shows today is a present state.

changes.was: about four fifths or a little more by the vintage
changes.now: about four fifths by the house's sheets for the 2013 and the 2015
changes.why: 85 per cent for the 2013 and 78 for the 2015 by the house; the vintages quoted are named.
sources: Philipponnat: the 2015 vintage in the spotlight

changes.was: named for its pale colour; the 2007, 2008 and 2015 are among those sold
changes.now: the 2007, 2008 and 2012 are among the vintages sold
changes.why: The naming rests on Decanter alone; a 2015 Juste Rosé was not found, the 2012 is sold by Berry Bros. and Rudd and Justerinis.
sources: Berry Bros. and Rudd: Philipponnat Clos des Goisses Juste Rosé 2012
Justerinis: Clos des Goisses Juste Rosé 2012

changes.was: so it has sun from sunrise to sunset; at 10 to 12 degrees
changes.now: enclosed by a wall since 1887; at 9 to 12 degrees
changes.why: No source read carries the sun's hours; the wall is the house's; the temperature now agrees with cuvee.serve.

open: NM was not read on a label: no label code was found; the Union lists the house among its members and it buys fruit beyond its vines.
The 1912 purchase of the Vallet cellars rests on the author's reading; this refuter's search of the house's own domain did not return it.
The Clos's size is 5.83 hectares by the house and 5.5 by the Union and Decanter; the record keeps the house's figure.
